questions.explanation: Zero conditional for general truths: if + present, present.
questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.

questions.explanation: First conditional for real future possibilities: if + present, will.
questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.

questions.explanation: Second conditional for unreal present: if + past simple, would.
questions.q: If I ___ rich, I'd travel the world.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: if + present simple in both clauses.
questions.q: Plants die if you ___ water them.

questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + infinitive.
questions.q: If she studies hard, she ___ the exam.

questions.explanation: Second conditional gives advice about an unreal situation: would + infinitive.
questions.q: If I were you, I ___ to the doctor.

questions.explanation: First conditional: no 'will' in the if-clause.
options: If it will rain, we'll stay home.
If it rains, we'd stay home.
If it rains, we'll stay home.
If it would rain, we'll stay home.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.
questions.q: If we ___ earlier, we wouldn't be late.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional for facts: present simple in both parts.
questions.q: If you mix red and yellow, you ___ orange.

questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, not 'won't'.
questions.q: She'll be angry if you ___ her the truth.

questions.explanation: Second conditional questions use 'would'.
questions.q: What ___ you do if you saw a ghost?

questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple for unreal present situations.
questions.q: If they ___ harder, they'd win more matches.

questions.explanation: 'Unless' + present simple takes 'will' in the main clause (first conditional).
questions.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional for scientific facts: present simple.
questions.q: If water ___ 100°C, it boils.

questions.explanation: Never use 'would' in the if-clause: 'If I had time'.
options: If I had time, I'd help you.
If I have time, I'll help you.
If I would have time, I'd help you.
If I had had time, I'd have helped you.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.
questions.q: He wouldn't be so tired if he ___ to bed earlier.

questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple for a real future result.
questions.q: If you ___ smoke, you'll feel better.

questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple for unreal present wishes.
questions.q: I'd buy a bigger house if I ___ more money.

questions.explanation: Second conditional advice: 'If I were you, I'd...'.
options: If I am you, I would accept.
If I were you, I will accept.
If I were you, I'd accept.
If I would be you, I'd accept.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, no 'will' in the if-clause.
questions.q: If it ___ snowing, we'll go skiing.
